summary: Using MATLAB, we developed a geochemical matching model that calculates standardized Euclidean distances across organic carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus, and pH to identify Earth locations with soil profiles analogous to the Moon and Mars. By pinpointing these terrestrial testbeds—such as sites in New Zealand, the UK, and China—this research enables controlled soybean cultivation experiments, supporting sustainable astronaut nutrition and psychological well-being during long-duration space missions.
details:
1. What does it do / How does it work?
  • Compares Earth soil data against Moon and Mars reference targets for organic carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus, and pH.
  • Uses MATLAB to calculate standardized Euclidean distances and rank top analog testbeds like New Zealand, the UK, India, China, Germany, and Sweden.
2. What benefits does it have?
  • Provides accessible Earth testbeds for nutrient-dense, nitrogen-fixing soybeans without needing rare space regolith.
  • Supports astronaut mental health through live plant care and combats menu fatigue with fresh harvests.
3. What is the intended impact of the project?
  • Enables sustainable, self-sufficient food production for permanent Moon bases and Mars missions.
  • De-risks future off-world agriculture while protecting crew nutrition and behavioral health.
4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?
  • MATLAB for data import, standardization, and Euclidean distance modeling.
  • NASA Earthdata (ORNL DAAC), *Lunar Sourcebook*, Mars Phoenix Lander data, and geographic mapping software.
5. How is your project creative?
  • Connects space agriculture to both physical nutrition and astronaut psychological well-being.
  • Frames complex geochemical modeling around the memorable *"Error 404: Earth Not Found"* mission theme.
6. What factors did your team consider?
  • Geochemical soil parameters (OC, N, P, pH), soybean optimal growth conditions, and extreme space environments.
  • NASA behavioral health standards and model limitations like equal variable weighting.
